Not changed: writes accepts directories, and a package-level write scope is the intended remedy for dependent files the design cannot enumerate; file-level writes are an author's choice that trades amendments for precision. Guidance, no detector: whether gates must be green after every step is a repository principle the validator cannot read. v2-authoring.md now says to keep red oracles in the base runs OD-75 requires rather than in early steps when the repository demands per-step green gates.

Not changed: the producer's prose is the exported contract, so a fingerprint that ignored wording would miss a wording change that alters meaning. Editorial notes belong in Clarifications, which fingerprints do not read; a superseded sentence is removed or rewritten with a version bump.

Not supported now: a consume edge outside a program would need a second ordering and pinning path. A standalone or cross-program consumer pins the producer fingerprint in prose and covers each reliance with a preflight item (relies_on), which preflight already requires.

## OD-71 program write-owner check forbids serial children that edit one package

Observed 2026-09-26 authoring `docs/rpc/rpc-program.sdd.md` (migai): six children form a strict
`depends_on` chain (merge → layering → error-format → control → ipc-plugins/process) and each edits
`packages/rpc` after its predecessor is verified. `validate` reported `SDD_V2_OWNER_CONFLICT:
write-owner-conflict` for every pair (v2-document.ts:751-760 compares all child write pairs with no
regard to `depends_on`), so a legitimately sequential migration program cannot use `sdd-program/v2`;
the author had to downgrade the root to a document-only roadmap and lose root-level
Entry/Asset/integration checks. The check models children as parallel; a detector would exempt
pairs where one child transitively depends on the other (serial ownership) and still flag overlap
between children in the same dependency layer.
**Class:** gate-scope
Fixed 2026-09-27: `scripts/validator/domain/v2-document.ts` skips write pairs whose owners are
ordered by transitive `depends_on` (reusing `ancestors` from `v2-tasks.ts`); unordered overlaps are
still reported. Regression: `tests/v2-boundaries.test.ts` "OD-71" (red on the old check: five
conflicts including every serial pair; green after: only the unordered b–d overlap).

## OD-72 preflight links workspace node_modules so cross-package patches never take effect

Observed 2026-09-26 preparing `docs/rpc/rpc-merge.bc1.patch` (migai, pnpm workspace): `linkInstalled`
symlinks each package's whole `node_modules` directory into the disposable tree; pnpm's workspace
links inside it (`@migaia/web-rpc -> ../../../web-rpc`) then resolve against the real repository,
so a patch that changes package A and asserts the effect from package B's tests runs B against the
unpatched A and fails (or passes) for the wrong reason. Workaround used: the item command first
deletes the tree's `node_modules` symlinks and runs `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`
inside the tree. A fix would materialise workspace packages' `node_modules` as real directories with
workspace links re-pointed into the tree, or document the workaround in the preflight item guide.
**Class:** feasibility
Addendum 2026-09-26: the workaround must also `git rm --cached` each linked `node_modules` path —
`materialise` commits the symlinks because a `node_modules/` ignore pattern does not match a
symlink, so deleting them leaves tracked-but-missing paths that break any build step that lists
`git ls-files --cached` (observed: migai `scripts/dist-stamp.mjs`).

## OD-73 `--replay` cannot run workspace oracles that need built dists

Observed 2026-09-26 (migai, `docs/serialize/serialize-optional-peers.sdd.md` closure by codex): the
replay exports each tree with `git archive` and links installed `node_modules`, but a pnpm workspace
package's oracle needs (a) built `dist/` of itself and its workspace deps (vitest dist-freshness
guard, `pnpm pack` in A3) and (b) workspace links that point into the exported tree (OD-72). A1/A3/A4
passed in the working tree and at the change commit but were `environment-failed` under replay, so
the host could not record a replay. The same class also produced two authoring gaps the checks did
not catch before handoff: an acceptance whose red state is created by one step and turned green by
another must map the requirement to both steps (`R2: no implementing file changed`), and an existing
test chosen as a preserve oracle must be listed in the step `touches`/`writes` that adds its case
marker. A detector would warn when an oracle's package has a `build` script and dist-freshness guard
and no replay preparation command is declared, and when a preserve oracle file lies outside `writes`.
**Class:** feasibility
Addendum 2026-09-27 (rpc-layering closure by codex): the same oracle-link rule forced edits outside
`writes` in a second package — store-worker `exports.test.ts` already asserted A9 but its describe
title lacked `A9`, so closure could not link the oracle until the host renamed the title. A detector
would accept an explicit oracle file/test path from the acceptance row instead of requiring the
acceptance ID inside a test title.
Second-order effect observed the same day: codex prefixed two `scripts/test/error-registry.test.mjs`
titles with `A5` for linking, and the merge A6 oracle masks exactly those tests by title
(`permittedA5Titles`), so A6 started failing silently outside any gate the closure ran.

## OD-74 closure symbol probe cannot see symbols defined in dependency packages

Observed 2026-09-27 closing `docs/rpc/rpc-layering.sdd.md` (migai, by codex): S5's pseudocode calls
`attachErrorIdentity`, which already exists in `packages/utils/src/error.ts` and is imported by the
change. Closure reported it as an unimplemented symbol because the probe scans only the SDD's
`writes` and Bundle `reads`. Adding utils as a read source did not help, so the host rewrote the
code fence as prose ("equivalent call description") only to silence the probe, which lowers the
design's precision. The same false positive hit `import` inside S1 pseudocode of
`serialize-optional-peers` (OD-73 run). A detector would resolve a probed symbol through the
repository's import graph (or accept any workspace definition) and would skip keywords and
comments inside fences.
**Class:** gate-scope

## OD-75 preflight never confirms acceptance polarity at base

Observed 2026-09-26/27 (migai). (a) `rpc-layering` A1 was authored as a change acceptance
(base FAIL, change PASS) but passes at base; this surfaced only at closure, and the host had to
reclassify A1 as preserve. (b) `rpc-merge` A11 treated `packages/web-rpc` `test:packed` as a

Seven review rounds read these oracles but never ran them. A detector would make preflight run
every named oracle at base once and fail when a change acceptance passes or a preserve acceptance
fails there.

## OD-77 preflight digest binds the whole SDD, so implementation records invalidate it

Observed 2026-09-26/27 (codex, `rpc-layering` and `rpc-merge` closure): every Clarifications entry
the host is required to add (implementation records, closure index corrections) changed the SDD
digest and made the preflight report stale (`SDD_V2_PREFLIGHT_STALE`). The host ran
`preflight --affected` at least four times during one closure although no preflight item, patch or
acceptance changed. A detector would digest only the clauses a preflight item depends on
(requirements, BC rows, acceptance, preflight items) and ignore append-only Clarifications.
**Class:** blast-radius
Recurred 2026-09-29 (codex, migai `rpc-error-format` I3 delivery): implementation-time
corrections took the leaf from revision 7 to 18 and the program root from 5 to 19 in about two hours;
each append-only record staled the report and `--affected` re-ran every gate item, so one step (S1)
cost over two hours until the user told the host to run preflight only at leaf start and end.

## OD-79 closure accepts a host-chosen gate subset; repository gates the change breaks stay unrun

Observed 2026-09-27 auditing codex's `rpc-layering` closure (migai, `2c43521`): `validate --evidence`
returned CLOSED, but `typecheck:e2e` (33 errors: `e2e/fixtures/*` still imported `IWebRpc*` names
the BC2 rename removed), `test:packed` (`packed-export-smoke.mjs` still read `isWebRpcError`,
`IWebRpcFeature*`, `IWebRpcFactoryConfig`, and a legacy fixture imported `WebRpcError`) and
`coverage:custody` (rpc branches covered 3119 → 3090 after dead-code deletion, baseline never
re-signed) all failed. The predecessor `rpc-merge` listed those three gates; the layering SDD's §9
silently dropped them, and neither authoring review nor closure compared the gate list with the
package's own scripts or with repository gates whose inputs the change edits (coverage baseline
after deleting code). A detector would derive a minimum gate set from the touched packages'
`package.json` scripts (every `typecheck:*`, `test*`) plus repository gates reading touched paths,
and would refuse CLOSED while any of them lacks a PASS row or an explicit exclusion.
**Class:** gate-scope

## OD-80 migration preflight cannot exercise structural moves, only BC candidate patches

Observed 2026-09-26 implementing `rpc-merge` S5 (codex): widening `tsconfig.json#include` to `src`
applied `verbatimModuleSyntax` to `discovery-attachment.ts`, whose all-inline-`type` import then
survived as an empty runtime import and added a graph edge that
`core-retained-causal.test.ts:130` forbids. Preflight had passed because its items patch only BC
rows (the `source` value); the relocation and config rewrite could not be tried before
implementation, so the host stopped for a user ruling. A detector would allow a migration SDD to
declare a scripted structural preflight (move plus config rewrite in the disposable tree) and run the
preserve suite against it.
**Class:** feasibility

## OD-81 file-level `writes` has no implementation-time amendment path

Observed 2026-09-29 (codex, migai `rpc-error-format` I3, ledger K68, K72, K76, K80, K81): every file
the design missed (an exhaustive `Record` text map, a test title map, a new file's custody baseline,
two internal reporter paths) forced an SDD edit and a revision bump before the host could touch it,
because the step gates and preflight `writes_outside` treat an unlisted file as a violation. The
checks cannot tell a design error from an omitted dependent file. A fix would let the host record
dependent files in an append-only delivery section that the digest ignores and that the next
revision folds into `writes`, while `writes_outside` still fails for files outside that record.
**Class:** gate-scope

## OD-82 red-first steps contradict per-step green gates

Observed 2026-09-29 (codex, migai `rpc-error-format` S1/S2/S7/S8, ledger K78, K79): the leaf put red
oracles in S1 and registered new codes in S2 before any throw site existed, while the repository
requires `fmt → lint → typecheck → typecheck:test → test` to pass after every step; S1 could not pass
`typecheck:test` and the layering suite failed on codes without throw sites. The host reordered steps
and moved red oracles into preflight candidate patches. `validate` accepted the original order. A
detector would flag a step whose `closes` acceptance is red at that step when the principles demand
green gates per step, and would steer red oracles into preflight base runs.
**Class:** feasibility

## OD-83 export fingerprints hash clause prose, so wording fixes cascade through consumers

Observed 2026-09-28/29 (migai `rpc-error-format` R5, `supervision-*`, `event-subscriber-unique-admission`):
annotating a superseded sentence or renaming a key without semantic change changed the export
fingerprint, which staled every consumer pin and forced revision bumps in consumers and the program
root; one author kept a superseded sentence in R5 only to avoid the cascade. A fix would fingerprint
a normalized semantic projection (IDs, types, codes, acceptance links) or let the producer mark an
edit as editorial with a reviewer-checked reason.
**Class:** blast-radius

## OD-84 preflight commits with `--no-verify`, which host rules forbid

Observed 2026-09-29 (codex, migai I3): `scripts/preflight.ts:64,112` commit inside the disposable
tree with `--no-verify`; the repository rules (and the host prompt) forbid that flag, so the host
edited the shared skill script before every preflight run and restored it afterwards. The checks
cannot see that a skill script conflicts with host principles. A fix would disable hooks without the
flag (for example `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit`) and state in the README that disposable
commits never touch the user repository.
**Class:** feasibility

## OD-85 no structural consume across programs or from standalone leaves

Observed 2026-09-28/29 (migai `pipeline-internal-cleanup`, `rpc-listener-fanout`, `plugin-host-async-prepare`,
ledger K66, CR-29): a leaf consuming an export from another program or a standalone leaf must keep
`consumes` empty and pin the fingerprint in prose, because `validate` reports
`consumer-dependency-missing`; ordering and fingerprint drift then rely on manual review. A fix would
allow `consumes` to name a producer SDD path outside the program and check its fingerprint without
adding a program edge.
**Class:** gate-scope

## OD-86 clause anchoring picks the first table row that starts with the ID

Observed 2026-09-29 (migai `supervision-threads`, ledger K59): the fingerprint for R2–R9 hashed the
clause-mapping table in §0.1 (`| R2 | …`) instead of the normative R2 bullet, so edits to the real
requirement would not have staled consumers. The author escaped the table IDs with backticks as a
workaround. A fix would anchor only on the normative definition form (`- R2 …` in §1–§5) and report
ambiguous anchors.
**Class:** blast-radius
